topics.label: Introduction and Learning Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, outlines the scope of the cancer lecture series, and presents the session's learning outcomes.

topics.label: Origins of Cancer and the Balance Between Intrinsic and Environmental Risks
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the foundational biology of cancer development, debating the relative contributions of intrinsic random mutations, inherited predispositions, and environmental exposures supported by epidemiological data.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Carcinogenic Agents and Tumor Promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how specific biological, chemical, and physical agents induce carcinogenesis through direct mutagenic action, xenobiotic metabolic activation, or inflammatory tumor promotion across different tissues and life stages.

topics.label: Methodologies for Investigating and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the genomic, epidemiological, animal model, and in vitro experimental approaches used to identify mutational signatures and evaluate whether suspected agents are carcinogenic.

topics.label: Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Analysis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by summarising the challenges of establishing carcinogenicity and reflecting on everyday risk-benefit decisions regarding environmental exposures.
